**TL;DR** — Claude Code v2.1.224 lands a self-hosted runner and removes the subagent cap the same week a CVSS 9.8 Gitea RCE demands immediate action from anyone running it.

## Anthropic and Claude

- **Claude Opus 5 launched July 24** as a "step change" for long-running agents — 1M-token context, $5/$25 per Mtok (same as Opus 4.8), now the default Opus model in Claude Code. Benchmarks show ~2x improvement over 4.8; excels at coding, chemistry, and visual artifacts. [source](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-opus-5)
- **Claude Code v2.1.224 (Aug 7)**: self-hosted runner via `claude self-hosted-runner` (Team/Enterprise), cross-session `SendMessage`/`ListAgents` on macOS/Linux, sandbox credential masking with JWT decode and AWS SigV4 re-signing, and the 200-subagent-per-session cap is gone. [source](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog)
- **v2.1.223 (Aug 6) patched three sandbox escapes**: bash permission bypass via crafted commands, dynamic `import()` escaping the script sandbox, and `bypassPermissions` ignoring org disable policy — worth reviewing if you run Claude Code in multi-user or CI contexts. [source](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog)
- **Fable 5 biology safeguards tightened (Aug 7)** — Anthropic updated biosafety mitigations on the Fable 5 model following its own cybersecurity/biology evaluation work (see Jul 30 incident report). [source](https://www.anthropic.com/news)
- **Daring Fireball (Aug 2)** covered Boris Cherny's account of directing Claude Code to rewrite the Claude desktop app in Swift via GitHub runners — still running after two weeks, with "questionable design outcomes." Interesting real-world stress-test of long-running agent workflows. [source](https://daringfireball.net/)

## NixOS Ecosystem

- **NixOS 26.05 "Yarara"** (May 30, ongoing) is the current stable release, maintained through December 2026. Nothing new on the NixOS blog in the last 7 days. [source](https://nixos.org/blog/)
- **Documentation team funding drive** (Jul 10) — NixOS Foundation is seeking community funding to hire paid doc maintainers and evaluate documentation frameworks; worth watching if you rely on nixpkgs docs. [source](https://nixos.org/blog/)
- Nothing genuinely new from nixos.org in the past week — if you need nixpkgs PR activity, the GitHub repo is the current source.

## AI Coding Agents and Agent Frameworks

- **Supabase open-sourced Evals** (Apache-2.0, ~Aug 1) — a benchmark that scores Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode on real support tickets and GitHub issues, running inside Docker with actual MCP interfaces and LLM-as-judge scoring. First serious agent eval grounded in real product tasks rather than synthetic puzzles. *(Source outside approved set)* [source](https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/08/01/supabase-releases-evals-an-open-source-benchmark-that-scores-claude-code-codex-and-opencode-on-real-supabase-tasks/)
- **GPT-5.6 GA (Jul 9)** — OpenAI shipped it in three tiers (Sol, Terra, Luna); Codex now defaults to gpt-5.6-sol. Relevant competitive context as Claude Opus 5 also just landed. *(Source outside approved set — synthesized from search results)*
- **Subagent depth cap raised to 3** in Claude Code v2.1.219, alongside the full Opus 5 rollout — agents can now spawn nested subagents three levels deep by default, enabling more complex orchestration patterns. [source](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog)

## Self-Hosting and Homelab

- **Gitea CVE-2026-59774 (CVSS 9.8, Aug 2)** — unauthenticated Org-mode markup RCE on any public repository's render endpoint; self-hosters own the patch cycle here, update immediately. *(Source outside approved set)* [source](https://blog.elest.io/self-hosted-weekly-week-32-2026-proxmox-arm64-rust-ai-policy-gitea-cve/)
- **Proxmox VE 9.2 for arm64 (Aug 5)** — full feature parity with x86-64 (KVM, LXC, ZFS, Ceph), shared codebase and release lifecycle. Meaningful for anyone running ARM homelab hardware. *(Source outside approved set)* [source](https://blog.elest.io/self-hosted-weekly-week-32-2026-proxmox-arm64-rust-ai-policy-gitea-cve/)
- **OpenVPN patches (Aug 6)**: CVE-2026-63649 (Windows directory traversal bypass) and CVE-2026-63650 (certificate validation failure in mbedTLS builds) — patch if running OpenVPN server, especially on Windows. *(Source outside approved set)* [source](https://blog.elest.io/self-hosted-weekly-week-32-2026-proxmox-arm64-rust-ai-policy-gitea-cve/)

## Local and On-Device LLM Inference

- **GGUF Q4_K_M is the de facto standard** for local deployment (ongoing) — applies different compression ratios per layer ("k-quants"), cuts memory ~75% vs FP16, brings a 7B model from 16GB to ~4GB VRAM with near-negligible quality loss. Most open-source models now ship GGUF on release day. *(Source outside approved set)* [source](https://www.sitepoint.com/local-llms-are-getting-easier-the-complete-guide-2026/)
- **ExecuTorch 1.0 GA** (Meta, Oct 2025 — ongoing state-of-play): 50KB base footprint, 12+ hardware backends, 80%+ of popular edge LLMs on HuggingFace run out of the box; marks production readiness for on-device inference from microcontrollers to smartphones. *(Source outside approved set)* [source](https://www.aimagicx.com/blog/on-device-ai-models-local-llm-guide-2026)
- Nothing from the last 7 days rose above the noise on this topic — the landscape is consolidating around GGUF/llama.cpp/Ollama rather than seeing dramatic new releases this week.
